gaps.desktop: The text caret in the title field is cut short and runs into the text. In the loser it spans only ~26px (y75-101), starting ~2px above the ascenders, and its left edge overlaps the final 's' of 'Book hotels' by ~1px. The winner draws a full line-height caret (~31px, from ~7px above the ascender tops to ~5px below the baseline) with a clean ~2px gap after the last glyph, like a native NSTextView insertion point.
gaps.phone: The caret in the title field is shorter than the capital letters. In the loser it is only ~19px tall (y50-69), so its top sits ~2px below the cap height of the 'B' in 'Buy suitcase', and it overlaps the trailing 'e'. The winner's caret is ~24px (y45-69), rising ~3px above the caps like the native iOS insertion point, and sits flush against the glyph without overlapping it. (Minor: the loser's checkbox stroke is also paler, ~#BEBEBE against ~#B1B1B1.)

why: The two are pixel-identical in type, spacing, icons, card and shadow; the deciding detail is the caret: the winner's is full line-height and clear of the text, while the loser's is stubby and collides with the last letter.
